label: Companies House update · 18 November 2026
title: Companies House identity verification one year on: what to do if a director has still not verified
summary: The 12-month transition for existing directors ended on 17 November 2026. Companies House says enforcement is under way, with warning letters, prosecutions and planned notes on the public register.
body:
On 18 November 2026 Companies House marked one year of mandatory identity verification. The requirement started on 18 November 2025 and was phased in over 12 months for people who were already directors or people with significant control (PSCs). That transition is now over, and Companies House has made clear that it is moving on to enforcement.

Where things stand

  • Companies House says about 90% of live companies have complied, and more than 12 million appointments have been verified.
  • Its figures at 11 November 2026 show 88.1% of companies had met the requirements linked to their confirmation statement, and 11.4% were on a compliance or enforcement pathway.
  • By the end of March 2027, Companies House expects every company either to have met the requirements linked to its confirmation statement or to be on a compliance or enforcement pathway.

The deadlines that applied

  • Existing directors: verify alongside the company's confirmation statement due between 18 November 2025 and 17 November 2026.
  • Existing PSCs who are also directors: within 14 days of that confirmation statement due date.
  • Existing PSCs who are not directors: within 14 days of the start of their birth month.
  • New companies and new directors: a company cannot be incorporated, and a new director cannot be appointed, until the director has verified. New PSCs have 14 days.

What happens if someone has not verified

Companies House guidance says it is unlawful to act as a director without completing identity verification, and that if an individual is in breach, the company is also in breach. A PSC who does not verify may also be committing an offence.

  • Default letters: if a deadline is missed, Companies House sends a letter warning that enforcement may follow without further notice. Financial penalty warning letters began in July 2026.
  • Financial penalties: these can be issued to the company, to individual officers and to PSCs.
  • Prosecution and disqualification: Companies House reports 131 convictions for failing to file confirmation statements, with failure to verify treated as an aggravating factor. In September 2026 the Insolvency Service secured the first convictions and disqualifications for acting as a director with an unverified identity.
  • Public register: Companies House plans to add notes to the register for those who miss the legal deadline. It says further details will follow.

What I would do now

  • Check every director and PSC. Make sure each one has a Companies House personal code, including directors who live abroad and PSCs who are not involved day to day.
  • If someone missed the deadline, verify straight away. You can do it free through GOV.UK One Login, or through an Authorised Corporate Service Provider such as an accountant.
  • Read any letter from Companies House carefully. If there were exceptional circumstances, you can make a written representation, but only within the timeframe in the letter. Late representations are not considered.
  • PSCs: Companies House guidance allows a PSC to ask for an extension of up to 14 days in some cases.
